notes.title: VR Ping Pong Pro arrives on November 12th!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

We're super happy to let you know that we have a final release date for VR Ping Pong Pro! You will be able to serve up and jump in on November 12th via Steam and PlayStation 4!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/25438973/8870a70374f3bf9e3940cceda8a4c4eece452d27.gif[/img]

Keep an eye on here for more information soon and make sure to add the game to your wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1029730/VR_Ping_Pong_Pro/

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N8KjoKqkYoo

notes.title: New gameplay trailer for VR Ping Pong Pro!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We're thrilled to showcase a brand new gameplay trailer for VR Ping Pong Pro! This video dives into both customisation and some of the mini-games available on launch day for those looking to practice their serve in new and exciting ways!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35326082/58e85ce7f58f6325f352d93d19203a0a4894b65a.gif[/img]

There's a wealth of customisable rackets and balls available in VR Ping Pong Pro and we want you to play in a style that suits you best! Whether that's kicking back in our 'Wall Table Tennis' mini-game or testing out your new racket in our new 'Bowling' mini-game!

We'll have lots more content coming up over the next few weeks and building into launch with new screenshots, gifs and other exciting bits of information so keep an eye on the steam page for more! 

[previewyoutube=N8KjoKqkYoo;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: VR Ping Pong Turns Pro!
notes.notes:
[img]https://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/1029730/extras/VR_Ping_Pong_Pro_2.gif?t=1561710320[/img]
The follow up to the hit table tennis simulator of 2016, VR Ping Pong, is making its way onto PC VR in September. Test your skills with a variety of challenging game modes, as you rise up the ranks to become the true Ping Pong Pro! Do you have what it takes? Pick up your virtual racket and find out!
[img]https://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/1029730/extras/VR_Ping_Pong_Pro_1.gif?t=1561710320[/img]
Featuring eight new levels including an arcade, a stadium and a Japanese garden; you can compete to become the champion against gorgeous and photorealistic backdrops! VR Ping Pong Pro also features racket/ball customisation with a tonne of different options to choose from; you can become the pro in style!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1783637420
Go from novice to pro with five unique difficulty levels to suit any player’s skill level. The addition of in-depth player statistics, online rankings and online multiplayer raises the stakes as you all compete to become the true Ping Pong Pro – after all, there can only be one! Will it be you?

Check out the VR Ping Pong Pro page now!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1029730/VR_Ping_Pong_Pro

[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/970997966313193481/393C4BEEC63587F101C30B15C6E767B01C07F127/[/img]

Keep up to date by joining our [b]Discord Server[/b] and following [b]#VRPingPongPro[/b]
[url=https://discord.gg/merge]https://discord.gg/merge[/url]

notes.title: More Updates! Leaderboard, Height and Distance Options!
notes.notes:
Hi VR Ping Pong Enthusiasts!

Thanks for all the comments on social media and the community hub here on Steam.

We've been listening carefully to what you have been saying. The most common questions we get are:
[list][*]The table is too low!
[*]The table is too high!
[*]I'm too close to the table!
[*]I'm stuck inside the table! :P[/list]

Well this update is for you! Introducing: Player Height and Distance Settings! :D

[img]http://i.imgur.com/4CZEWjp.gif[/img]

[b]What's new in this update:[/b]
[list][*]Wall-mode Leaderboard
[*]Ability to choose the player's height relative to the table.
[*]Ability to choose the player distance from the table. (Depth)
[*]New 11-0 Achievement (Win a set 11-0)[/list]

[b]Bug fixes:[/b]
[list][*]Ball Colors
[*]Edge shots[/list]

Bonus gif! Previously, we had the option to rotate the paddle. Here's how:

[img]http://i.imgur.com/F0dMwJe.gif[/img]

notes.title: Feedback and Early Access
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone,

Just a reminder that VR Ping Pong is in Early Access meaning you can shape the game as final touch ups are made going into full release.

Please let us know if you have any thoughts on anything in the game. Tell us what you like, don't like, any bugs. We'll see what we can do here on the Community Hub:

http://steamcommunity.com/app/492710/discussions/

If you have a big list of things, make a new discussion thread and we can get in depth with replies.

Of course, we will be posting updates so you can keep track of how things are coming along. We'll have changelogs for updates so you know if your suggestion made it to the game.

Thanks for your interest and support for VR Ping Pong!

- James

notes.title: Ping Pong Physics!
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone,

So we've been talking about the game in various social networks and the question that comes up often is: What are the physic like? Well, let's crunch some variables!

[h1]About Physics[/h1]
Our physics system is designed to simulate the best ping pong experience possible in VR. To do this we had to modify standard nVidia PhysX behaviour to add two important things:

[list]
[*][u]Motion[/u]: When players perform a backspin or a topspin in our system the ball takes an angular velocity that, based on the direction and the velocity of the paddle, modify the bounce and the behaviour of the ball in the air. 
[/list]

In real life this behaviour is given by the friction of the ball on the paddle: in a fraction of a second the ball (due to its deformation) stays in contact with the paddle and this friction, combined with the velocity of the paddle, produce the angular velocity (usually called EFFECT).
To implement this, our approach was little bit different: we haven't got ball deformation on contact so we haven't the friction for that change; to solve this problem we have calculated the correct exit angular velocity by the velocity of the paddle and the normal vector of the impact (multiplied for a constant to adjust the effect).

[list]
[*][u]Magnus Effect[/u]: in physics, the Magnus Effect occurs when a ball (a body in general) has an angular velocity and a velocity in a fluid. This effect is responsible of the change of the trajectory of the body. 
[/list]

When a body rotates in a fluid, it drags the nearest layer of fluid, this layer does the same thing and in this way, around the body, layers are formed like in fluid, that rotate by in concentric circumferences.
The force produced is similar to the lift effect on a plane, then the trajectory of the ball changes in the time.
To implement this effect, we constantly add a force to the ball that is the result of cross product of velocity and angular velocity multiplied for a constant to adjust the effect.

[h1]About AI[/h1]
There are two important things about the opponent AI:

[list]
[*][u]Prediction of the player’s shot[/u]: our AI system for prediction is divided into two parts:
a) The ball is hit by the paddle
b) The ball hits the table
The core of how the AI system works is in the equations of motion:
x=x0 + v0x*t
z=z0 + v0z*t
y=y0 + v0y*t + 1/2*g*t^2
these three equations describe how the ball moves over the time based on initial velocity and gravity: for efficiency purpose we haven't added into these equations air friction and the Magnus Force (above equations become differential equations with no constant force, like gravity).
When the ball is hit by the paddle, the opponent AI waits a fraction of second and then solves the y equation replacing the ball’s vertical velocity, y value with y0 and table height instead of y. In this mode we can obtain WHEN the ball will hit the table and WHERE (x, z): this information is very important to understand if the player's shot will hit the table.
When the ball hits the table, the AI system waits a fraction of second and then calculates how much time the ball consumes to arrive on the highest quota. Obtained this time we can calculate WHERE the paddle will be moved to hit the ball. Considering that the equations treat the ball movement like a movement in space, there is an error in this prediction: to avoid the paddle moves in a wrong position, the last algorithm is repeated every tick (not every frame).
There are other little adjustments that AI does to seem more human but can be left out because these aren't the core of AI system.
[/list]

[list]
[*][u]Choice of the shot[/u]: the algorithm that calculates where the shot will go is based on the same equations. A point on the table (or near the table) is chosen, with a dedicated algorithm, and a TIME for the shot is chosen: the point of the time is the core of the algorithm because less time means a more powerful hit was made, more time mean a less powerful hit was made. Also in this case the equations don't consider other forces (there is an algorithm that decides the angular velocity) and there is a little intentional error: it introduces variables closer to the human behaviour.
[/list]
